role: Analyst independent code/preparation reviewer; no implementation context
disposition: No blocking finding in the frozen preparation. Root may separately select the exact frozen collector after its own source preflight. This report itself neither selects nor runs the capture.

review_scope.fresh_selected_metadata: Read all seven selected record_metadata and alias/locator envelopes in the two pinned metadata gates; independently joined exact entries, extent, rows, thunk and export/warning qualification. Read the retained earlier base-return preparation plan as data for inherited image/header/TEXT identity provenance.
review_scope.fresh_code_review: Traced command dispatch, fixed selection digest/ranges, metadata and preparation preflight, exclusive destination, image/tool/provider watch, header/mapping/extraction, child invocation and cleanup, row equality, receipts and caught-failure paths through every new script function.
review_scope.inherited_semantics: Class/base source semantic findings and raw-record/alias/chunk correctness remain the explicitly pinned prior independent reviews. No new C-body, raw corpus, alias census, native window or encountered target was opened or semantically rederived.
review_scope.governance: Analyst-only fixed-selection independent review; frozen/canonical/shared data remain immutable. Root owns source preflight, actual selection, adoption, logs and any successor.

exact_seals.preparation_inventory: Exact four payloads and manifest verified independently; no added file. All seven provider byte/hash pairs independently verified.
exact_seals.preservation: Twelve unique preparation/selected-provider files were hashed before and after the data-only check and remained identical. The exclusive future capture destination remained absent. The report is the only file authored by this review.

guard_findings: Dispatch admits only --check or --capture-selected-once followed by the exact frozen selection digest; selection() independently verifies those selection bytes. No range/path/decoder overrides or retry mode exist.

validate_ranges first requires the exact ordered seven (entry,byte-count) tuples. It then checks start equals entry, four-byte alignment, exact end/length, bytes/4 rows, nonoverlap and 996/249 totals. An outside, duplicate, reordered or overlapping selection cannot satisfy this gate; the executed negative-control coverage is listed separately, not overstated as every possible corruption.

metadata verifies seven provider byte/hash pins, then each selected metadata record's exact interval, body length, thunk flag, zero warnings and complete/exported status. In particular the expanded projected C at 0x10215f3d8 yields only its four-byte physical thunk interval, not another 248-byte implementation.

The actual path requires -B and exclusively mkdir's the fixed v1 sibling. Existing failed or successful destinations refuse reuse; every receipt/raw output is opened xb. There is no automatic cleanup that erases partial failure evidence and no automatic retry.

The actual preflight checks exact preparation file-name inventory and all four payload pins. It watches only those five preparation files, seven selected providers, image and tool (14 unique files), not a prior universe. A separately selected invocation must pin the reviewed manifest/script externally: the collector does not embed an expected preparation-manifest SHA constant.

Future image/tool hashes are freshly checked once before and once after the batch. Header and 53/6944-byte load-command identities are parsed/checked before extraction; the after complete-image identity protects those bytes too, rather than a second explicit header/TEXT parse. Each window must fit exactly one mapping equal to the pinned __TEXT geometry/protections and fit physical image bounds.

Only seven exact windows are read into seven raw files. Each fixed argv invokes the existing Rizin on one raw file, explicitly arm/64/little, mapped to its selected start and pdj bytes/4. There is no shell, old collector import, callee/branch/global/slot traversal, original invocation, installation or analysis command.

At most seven sequential Popen attempts exist. Each uses core limit 0, a new session/process group, cwd fixed destination, stdout/stderr pipes, PID/PGID and UTC receipts. A timeout/nonzero exit/parse or byte failure stops the outer batch; no retry path exists.

Each decoder result must have the exact row count and selected raw length, consecutive integer offsets at four-byte spacing, size 4, nonempty/non-invalid opcode, non-ill type and four-byte hex for each row. Concatenated row bytes must equal the selected extraction exactly. This validates retained row/byte association; it does not independently prove decoder semantics, native control flow or ABI.

Each caught decoder path attempts process-group SIGKILL, captures/drains partial stdout/stderr, records return code/error/timeout/cleanup and writes completion UTC. Outer caught failures retain partial evidence, then attempt after-identities and final status.

check.limits: Synthetic validator and retained metadata checks only; not capture authorization, native ABI evidence or readiness approval.

operational_limits: Only the inspected data-only --check was executed. No Rizin startup, timeout behavior, process-group cleanup, image/tool read, Mach-O parsing on the real image, extraction, real decoder output or native ABI interpretation was tested in this review.

The 30-second timeout starts at communicate() after Popen returns. Cleanup may add two five-second waits; process creation/preexec, hashing, filesystem I/O and OS-uninterruptible operations are outside a hard whole-run deadline.

Process-group SIGKILL targets the dedicated child group, including descendants still in it; descendants which independently escape by creating another session/group are outside that guarantee. The fallback closes inherited pipes and waits for the direct child, not arbitrary escaped processes.

Catchable Python exceptions and normal KeyboardInterrupt/SIGTERM paths are handled where execution reaches the catch/finally blocks. SIGKILL, process/host crash, power loss, repeated interruption during cleanup, or failure before a child PID becomes available can prevent complete cleanup or receipts. No unconditional child/receipt guarantee is claimed.

Files are individually flush/fsync'd and exclusively created; the directory is not fsync'd. Disk-full, denied access, media errors, interruption during write or other filesystem failures can leave a partial receipt/tree and can prevent failure/status receipts themselves. Such a destination remains consumed and must not be retried automatically.

The collector inherits its outer environment and stdin and does not record them itself. Root has separately proposed minimal PATH/LANG/LC_ALL/TZ, isolated -I -B Python, stdin DEVNULL and core0 with an outer argv/environment receipt. Those are coordinator launch obligations, not behavior validated by this preparation review.

Pins and before/after identities establish checked immutable-file association for this local workflow, not adversarial concurrent-mutation resistance or a stable snapshot under changes which are made and restored between checks.
scope_exclusions: No actual capture flag, selected image/tool/window reads, native/provider/original execution, old collector imports/runs, decoder child, runtime harness, comparator/model, fixtures, build, new source expansion, frozen/shared mutation or publication.
